records.title: Skillo: A Predictive Artificial Intelligence Framework for Detecting Invisible Learning Gaps in Online Education
records.reason: The problem with using traditional assessment systems is that they rely on quizzes, which are not always a true indicator of conceptual understanding, and may obscure the invisible learning gap – when students are doing well while not learning. In this paper, we present Skillo, an adaptive learning platform with integrated AI capabilities designed to identify and bridge these unknown gaps by leveraging a multi-model pipeline that integrates the following models: BERT-based semantic similarity model [13], XGBoost classification model [12], and a Recommender based on RAG. The system features separate teacher and student portals, backed up by FastAPI, MongoDB and FAISS. The model is trained on 2,290 attempts by students from 50 topics and detects semantic and behavioural features of the attempted topics to identify students who have a lack of knowledge and understanding despite being awarded a score. Results show that Skillo provides possibilities for timely personalised interventions and helps to make formative assessment more effective in e-learning contexts.

records.title: Hierarchical Reasoning and Evidence-Guided Agentic Framework for Factual Text Summarization
records.reason: The growing use of abstractive text summarization in news, scientific literature, and multi-document analysis has increased the need for summaries that contain factual information supported by their sources. Recent Transformer-based summarization models generate fluent and coherent summaries, but they often include hallucinated information, particularly in long and multi-document settings. Existing factuality-guided frameworks improve consistency using verification and refinement techniques, but most approaches rely on static pipelines and limited reasoning capabilities. In this work, we propose a Hierarchical Reasoning and Evidence-Guided Agentic Framework (HREAF) for factual text summarization. The framework retrieves supporting evidence, analyzes relationships among facts, generates summaries using fact planning, verifies factual correctness, and improves uncertain content through iterative refinement. Unlike earlier methods, the framework identifies uncertain parts of the summary and improves them using supporting evidence through multiple refinement steps. Experimental evaluation on the CNN/DailyMail, WikiSum, Multi-News, and DUC datasets demonstrates remarkable improvements in factual-consistency metrics, with FactCC scores of $\text{0. 9 4}, \text{0. 9 2}, \text{0. 9 3}, \text{0. 9 1}$, compared to strong baseline models. It also maintains competitive ROUGE performance with an R-L score of 43.6 on the CNN/DailyMail dataset. Ablation results demonstrate that iterative refinement is the most influential component, improving FactCC by 0.15, while hierarchical reasoning increases factual consistency by 0.07.
